World Series of Darts: Dubai Darts Masters will to return to PDC calendar in 2027 after 10-year absence

The World Series of Darts will return to Dubai for the 2027 season; the Dubai Darts Masters has not been played since 2017; Gary Anderson was the last player to win the title in Dubai; watch the World Championship live on Sky Sports

Tuesday 24 November 2026 08:11, UK

The World Series of Darts will return to Dubai in 2027, with the Dubai Darts Masters set to be played for the first time in 10 years.

Dubai was one of the tour's original destinations and had previously hosted a World Series event between 2013 and 2017.

The World Series will kick off its 2027 season in Bahrain on January 15, before heading to the United Arab Emirates for the Dubai Darts Masters.

- Darts in 2026: Key dates, calendar, results 📅

The tournament will see eight of the world's top PDC players battle it out in a 16-player knockout event between January 22 and 23 at the Coca-Cola Arena.

Scotland's Gary Anderson successfully defended his Dubai Darts Masters title when it was last held in 2017, beating Michael van Gerwen 11-7 in the final.

PDC chief executive Matt Porter said: "We're delighted to be taking the World Series of Darts back to Dubai.

"The city has a great history with the series, and Coca-Cola Arena will provide a brilliant setting for two days of top-class darts.

"We're looking forward to welcoming the world's best players and fans from across the region."

Eight first-round matches will be played on the opening night, before the knockout stages and the final are played on day two.

World Series ranking points will be up for grabs, as players look to secure their spots at the season-ending Finals in Amsterdam.

Ross Smith is out to defend his title after he thrashed Gerwyn Price 11-5 to become the 2026 World Series of Darts Finals champion in September, winning his second PDC major.

Sky Sports remains the home of darts with the World Championship (December 11-January 3) live.

item.title: Smith: I want to play on the PGA Tour
item.description:
【AI 精简版】 AI-trimmed version. An LLM deleted boilerplate sentences from the original article and left the rest verbatim. The original link at the end is the only authoritative source.

Why it is here: News of a player's career move with potential impact on future

Cameron Smith plots pathway back to the PGA Tour after moving on from LIV Golf

Cameron Smith joined LIV Golf in 2022 after clinching his first major at The Open at St Andrews; the Australian will play select events on the DP World Tour in 2027; watch Smith in action at this week's BMW Australian PGA Championship live on Sky Sports

Tuesday 24 November 2026 07:49, UK

Cameron Smith has moved on from LIV Golf, is preparing for his invitation-only appearances on the DP World Tour and is already thinking about a return to the PGA Tour.

As the 2022 British Open champion prepared for the BMW Australian PGA Championship starting Thursday at The Lakes in Sydney, attention inevitably turned to his career goals and his steps toward a possible return to the PGA Tour.

"I guess that's the path. That's where I want to be now for sure," Smith told the Australian Associated Press.

"DP's given us a chance to kind of fulfil that. We'll see how that goes. There's plenty of good players out there and plenty of other guys that want to do the same thing, so it's going to be difficult.

"But for sure that's where I want to play."

How can Smith return to the PGA Tour?

Smith will not return as a full-time member on the DP World Tour, but is one of a number of former LIV players, including Dustin Johnson and Bubba Watson, to sign an agreement with the tour to receive invites to a specific number of tournaments during the 2027 season, excluding Rolex Series events.

He receives an exemption to play this week, having won the BMW Australian PGA Championship three times in 2017, 2018 and 2022.

Under the DP World Tour and PGA Tour's current agreement, the top 10 players on the Race to Dubai Rankings qualify for the PGA Tour.

The number of PGA Tour cards available to players finishing at the top of the Race to Dubai Rankings for the 2028 season is yet to be determined, with the PGA Tour set to launch its new two-tier championship structure the year after next.

However, to even have a chance at winning one of those coveted cards, Smith will need to play more tournaments on the DP World Tour's 2027 schedule.

He could do that by winning the co-sanctioned BMW Australian PGA Championship or the Australian Open at Kingston Heath, which begins on December 3 and also features Rory McIlroy.

"I think given what they've told me, I pretty much need to win this year to get membership," Smith said.

"It's all still very blurry to me at the moment. There are a lot of rules, but we'll have a few opportunities, and like I said, I've always managed to play pretty good down here, so why not start it off with a good one?"

The PGA Tour board last week said it had "thoughtful discussions" about the future of players at LIV Golf but otherwise seemed to be in no hurry to decide if there is room for them next season.

CEO Brian Rolapp said the Returning Member Program, which allowed Brooks Koepka to return to the PGA Tour at the beginning of 2026 with financial penalties, was not on the table.

Smith didn't take up that one-time offer in January, which applied only to players who'd won majors or The Players Championship from 2022 through 2025, which included himself, Koepka, Jon Rahm and Bryson DeChambeau.

'It was a big move to go to LIV'

Smith is in a kind of limbo. LIV Golf, which lost the financial support of Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF) and filed for bankruptcy on September 8, told a bankruptcy court earlier this month it had abandoned plans for a new version of the league and had begun winding down its business.

"There was a lot of uncertainty and then in a way it was good to just like get the noise over and done with," Smith, who joined LIV after winning The Open at St Andrews in 2022, said.

"It was a big move to go LIV at the start for sure, and I think everyone that was close to me and all my friends saw why I was doing it and why I made the decision."

Adam Scott said he had no doubts about Smith fitting back in.

"Cam's incredibly talented and he'll adjust to his new environment," Scott said. "He'll be just fine."

item.description:

Why it is here: Analysis of current team performances in a competitive league

Wolves hit their stride, Stoke continue to dream but can they last the course and are QPR dark horses of Championship?

Wolves are improving defensively, Stoke look strong and QPR look resolute; Andy Hinchcliffe picks out the key stories in The Championship catch-up; a Sky Sports column focusing on the second tier.

Monday 23 November 2026 13:31, UK

Welcome to The Championship Catch-up, a new Sky Sports column in which Andy Hinchcliffe rounds up some of the key stories from the second tier. This week:

- Wolves are coming together under Peixoto

- Stoke look like they can last the course

- QPR's defensive improvements prove key

Wolves have added solidity at the back to attacking prowess

With the players Wolves have got and the way they play, they were always going to score goals. They've averaged around 1.7 goals per game across those periods, so they're still good for a goal under Cesar Peixoto.

But in the last seven games they've conceded only five, compared to the 14 goals they shipped in their first nine. They're not playing defensively, they're just defending well. They're keeping the ball and keeping teams away from their penalty area.

At the start of the season they were too open. They were great to watch and scoring goals, but conceding too many. They needed to find a balance. They didn't have to become ultra-defensive, but they did need some defensive strength.

They've got plenty of attacking threats. Raul Jimenez is still missing, but Adam Armstrong is doing really well and is a proven goalscorer at this level. They've got width, dynamism and options, while Andre plays a really important role sitting deep in midfield.

All I was looking for was more balanced performances. They didn't need to let the goals dry up just to keep clean sheets. They've managed to find that balance and do both. They're dominating games, keeping teams out and still scoring goals.

Even when they change the right-back, centre-half or left-back, they can maintain that defensive strength. They're clearly moving in the right direction and are now a much more balanced, complete team.

Kieran Trippier's experience has been invaluable. He cares about the club getting promoted back to the Premier League. Individually, he wants to do well, but he also wants the team to succeed.

He's perhaps not the player he was five years ago, but he can still have a huge effect. He'll have to get used to the fact that he might not play every game, but Wolves have the depth to manage that.

With Trippier, it's not just about his ability but also his leadership and experience. He can reinforce the standards they should be setting and what they're looking to achieve this season.

Latest Sky Sports deals or stream EFL games with no contract📺

Stoke City have won 10 of 16 games, more than any other Championship team. Would you have expected them to have won more games than Wolves, West Ham, Middlesbrough or Southampton after 16 matches? Probably not.

They're still overachieving in terms of the data, but Mark Robins spoke during the international break about the need to improve their performances. The league position doesn't really tell you how good you are. You have to monitor performances and look at how to develop and improve.

There's still work to do at both ends of the pitch, but they're getting goals from different players. George Hirst came in for big money and had been struggling for goals and not starting games. He won them the game against Birmingham, which is a lift for him and the team.

Against Birmingham, they were down to 10 men for a long time and showed the resilience to hold on to a 1-0 lead. When you look at everything, the foundations are there for them to get better.

How many experienced, very good coaches have gone to Stoke and not been able to make it work?

I just think it's wonderful that it's him because he's such a brilliant coach. He's very understated and humble. I saw him after a game recently and asked him a couple of tactical questions.

item.title: 'He's got to get 14 more to catch me!' - Taylor on Littler, crowds, and comeback
item.description:
【AI 精简版】 AI-trimmed version. An LLM deleted boilerplate sentences from the original article and left the rest verbatim. The original link at the end is the only authoritative source.

Why it is here: Interview with a sports personality discussing career and competition

Phil Taylor speaks on Luke Littler, crowds, and his sensational darting comeback ahead of MODUS Super Series return

Monday 23 November 2026 16:54, UK

Luke Littler has been the star of the darting show for what feels like an eternity - but Phil Taylor is in no doubt as to who still holds the crown.

The most decorated player in history will make a sensational return to the oche when Taylor joins up with long-time friend Adrian Lewis at the MODUS Super Series in his first competitive tournament in eight years, starting November 23 in Portsmouth.

The 16-time world champion has inevitably been compared to teenage sensation Littler - who already has two Alexandra Palace titles at 19 - but remains calm about the prospect of his world title record being overtaken.

- Darts in 2026: Key dates, calendar, results 📅

"I have more publicity [now] than when I was winning it!" Taylor joked, speaking to Sky Sports. "Everywhere I go, people ask me 'do think he'll beat your record? It's all debating all the time.

"He's got to get 14 more to catch me!

"So just to qualify for the next 14 years isn't easy. He's got to keep his form going, he's got to work hard, and even then, it'll take 14 years - that's if he wins it every year!"

"If the crowds keep on at him, then he might just walk away."

Taylor: Crowds are affecting Littler

Littler - the favourite in almost every tournament he participates in - has become something of a target of hostile darts crowds across the tour, even threatening to boycott future tournaments in the Netherlands after being booed and whistled during his defeat in World Series of Darts final in Amsterdam.

This is a feeling Taylor - who reached 14 consecutive World Championship finals between 1994 and 2007 - can relate to.

"I'm not a fan of it. I didn't like it when I was playing - it's the whistles," Taylor said.

"When you're in the venue, some of them are screaming and whistling and calling your every name under the sun. I have to go and get a dictionary when I get home to see what they were calling me!

"It is affecting him. He doesn't like it, and he doesn't deserve it in fairness.

"It's just something they keep saying you've got to get used to, but it's very, very difficult."

'Age has caught up with me'

Taylor left professional darts in show-stopping fashion, finishing runner up in the 2018 World Championship after a sensational run to the final as the No 6 seed.

Could the adrenaline of competitive darts tempt Taylor into a sensational return to the Pro Tour?

"No - I'm 66!" Taylor said emphatically.

"I've still got my own teeth, I've got my hip done, got my eyes done - but no, not a chance.

"It would be strange for me anyway, because I don't play competitive anymore. Adie [Adrian Lewis], still plays and it's going to be different. I'm just trying and trying and trying to pick my form up.

"Age has caught up with me, that's the problem."

Taylor and Lewis representing England is an image which will bring back fond memories for fans of a pairing that has won four World Cup of Darts titles - the most by any two players in the tournament's history.

It was the opportunity to share the stage with Lewis once again that was the deciding factor in tempting "The Power" back to the oche for one last dance.

"It was the owner of MODUS, Jason Thame, who said I was playing with Adie, and I said 'yeah, I'd enjoy that' - that's why I'm doing it!

"I'm not as good as what I used to be. He's going to have to really play well on this tournament, but I'm going to go and enjoy it. That's the main thing. We'll have a laugh."

item.title: Commanders upset Burrow's Bengals after last-second winner
item.description:
【AI 精简版】 AI-trimmed version. An LLM deleted boilerplate sentences from the original article and left the rest verbatim. The original link at the end is the only authoritative source.

Why it is here: NFL game summary with analysis of key plays and player performances

NFL: Washington Commanders beat Joe Burrow's Cincinnati Bengals in upset after last-second field goal from Drew Stevens

Tuesday 24 November 2026 06:34, UK

Jayden Daniels connected with rookie Antonio Williams on two long pass plays, moving the Commanders 64 yards in 34 seconds to set up Drew Stevens' 26-yard field goal as time expired as the Washington Commanders stunned Joe Burrow and the Cincinnati Bengals 22-20 on Monday night.

After Evan McPherson put the Bengals ahead 20-19 on a 56-yard field goal, Washington got the ball back with 39 seconds left and no timeouts.

Daniels hit Williams over the middle for 22 yards, spiked the ball, then found him again for a 42-yard catch-and-run to the Cincinnati eight. The Commanders quarterback spiked it with five seconds left and Stevens did the rest.

Daniels finished with 283 yards passing, Williams had nine catches for 122 yards, and Stevens was five for five on field goals as Washington (4-5-1) remained in the NFC East race, two games behind the division-leading New York Giants.

Washington's defense forced Burrow to settle for checkdowns all night.

The dangerous Bengals receiving duo of Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins combined for just seven catches for 74 yards.

Washington coach Dan Quinn made another questionable late-game decision when he sent Stevens out on fourth-and-one to kick a 41-yard field goal with 2:26 left for a 19-17 lead. That left plenty of time for Burrow, who found Mike Gesicki for a 32-yard completion to move the Bengals into field goal range.

A sack pushed the Bengals back, but McPherson nailed the long kick with 46 seconds remaining.

The game got off to a slow start in rainy conditions but opened up in the second half as the teams traded scores throughout the third quarter.

Burrow's four-yard touchdown pass to Colbie Young put the Bengals ahead 17-10, and the Commanders rallied with three field goals by Stevens.

There was an unexpected stoppage early in the third when the stadium lights went out with the Commanders in the red zone. After a delay that lasted about four minutes, Stevens converted from 36 yards to tie the game at 10-all.

Washington held Cincinnati to three points on its first four drives before Higgins' 31-yard touchdown catch that made it 10-0.

Dalton Smith: Paths align better for Shakur Stevenson unification than Adam Azim fight

Dalton Smith has had an outstanding 2026, winning and defending the WBC super-lightweight world title with wins over Subriel Matias and Alberto Puello; Smith believes he can headline at Hillsborough Stadium in his Sheffield hometown with American star Shakur Stevenson a potential opponent

Monday 23 November 2026 14:23, UK

Dalton Smith, the WBC super-lightweight champion, thinks he's more likely to fight Shakur Stevenson next than Adam Azim.

Sheffield's Smith has had an outstanding year, knocking out Subriel Matias in New York to win his world championship and defending the belt against Alberto Puello in his Sheffield hometown.

American star Shakur Stevenson secured the WBO's super-lightweight championship when he beat Teofimo Lopez in January.

Both Smith and Stevenson are looking for their next opponents and a unification between the pair would be an appealing match up.

"Boxing's business and if it makes good business on both sides it's definitely a fight that can be made. Obviously there's other champions, other belts. I just want to be part of the biggest fights," Smith told Sky Sports.

"It's a fight where the paths align a little bit better than me and Adam Azim right now. But like I said we'll see."

His advice to Azim is: "Be in world level fights.

"It's a fight what gets talked about a lot," Smith said of Azim. "I've got my own path I'm going on. I'm not just saying I'm doing. I think Adam needs to play his part as well.

"I'm not really concentrating on Adam. I'll let him do what he's doing.

"I'm concentrating on a big 2027 for me."

He would love to headline at Hillsborough Stadium in Sheffield next year.

"I'm in a position now to be part of some big, big fights," Smith said. "I'd love to have Hillsborough, I'd love to win more world titles.

"It's something I've dreamt of for years, I've always said it. People probably thought I was delusional at the time saying it, but I kept following the dream and I feel like it's very close. Possibly something we can get over the line next year. It'll just be big for Sheffield, big for the city and I'll be proud to say I've done it.

"I feel like I'm carrying that torch for the city now."
